hed: Joe diGenova resigns as DOJ counsel overseeing Florida probe of Trump investigators
dek: Joseph diGenova, the Trump ally tapped in April to oversee a Florida-based Justice Department inquiry into whether former intelligence and law-enforcement officials conspired against President Donald Trump, told Reuters and other outlets Thursday that he has resigned. ABC News first reported the departure; diGenova said it was an "honor and privilege" to serve the president and the department and declined to elaborate. CBS News reported he submitted his resignation letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche at 3 p.m. EDT and that his wife, attorney Victoria Toensing, who also worked with the Fort Pierce team, will leave Friday. The probe has issued recent grand-jury subpoenas but has not produced charges. A DOJ spokesperson did not immediately comment.

cl.body: Reuters, ABC News, and CNN frame the resignation as injecting uncertainty into a sprawling Florida probe of Trump's foes after clashes over pace and after diGenova lost the confidence of superiors; ABC said sources described White House and senior DOJ frustration that the "grand conspiracy" inquiry has produced no prosecutions.

cr.body: Fox News, Bloomberg, and CBS News report diGenova confirmed he resigned after sources said he had lost the confidence of the Justice Department and White House and had already been sidelined; CBS notes Toensing will also leave Friday, while the Florida grand-jury effort tied to Russiagate and related inquiries continues without charges so far.

seo_description: Joe diGenova says he resigned Thursday as the DOJ counsel overseeing a Florida probe of former officials who investigated Trump; ABC first reported the departure.
